description: The upgrade cycle's shared preset (ops docs/plans/120-automated-upgrade-cycle.md): Renovate finds the upgrades and
opens one branch per unit, the same name in infra, platform and ops; the cycle proves a unit on the Vagrant copy
(task test:copy:unit UNIT=<it>) and applies it - Renovate never merges. Units (scripts/upgrade-units.py reads these

names): renovate/wave-patches (every patch and digest, and every minor not a family's or a store's - operator 2026-11-23: one unit, not one each); renovate/<family>-<X.Y> for the families moved one minor at a time
(istio, kubernetes, cilium); renovate/<family> for the other families' minors (observability, data-operators, argocd,
pi-services); every major that can be undone on renovate/wave-majors (its newest only); a store's and a release line's major on a branch of its own (Renovate's own name). Label one-way: a change
its store cannot undo - the runner backs the store up first (scripts/upgrade-stores.json), or blocks it, naming the part with none.
A test environment's files: renovate/test-<unit>, merged before its production twin.

Every update waits on the dashboard for approval (operator 2026-11-24: dozens of open pull requests were noise): the runner ticks the one unit it would pick next (scripts/upgrade-units.py replenish) and runs Renovate again, so only the unit being worked on exists as pull requests. Pull requests opened before keep going until merged.

Renovate rebases a branch only on a conflict (rebaseWhen conflicted): infra's main moves many times a day by CD, and a rebase of every branch at every run was a queue of CI builds ahead of the apps' deploys - the cycle brings the one unit it picks onto main itself (Forgejo's update). No cap on pull requests: a cap per repo split one unit across the repos.
dependencyDashboardTitle: Upgrade cycle - Renovate's dashboard (label upgrades-paused: the cycle stops)

customManagers.description: Ansible version vars, each annotated on the line above it: '# renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<name> [registryUrl=<url>] [versioning=<v>]' - a registry or git-tags where the project publishes there (no token: Renovate refuses GitHub's API without one), versioning=semver where a registry's tags include bare minors (vault:1.22) - a value restating an Argo chart takes the chart's own datasource, name and repository, so its unit's branch is the one infra's chart gets

Images written as one string in values and manifests (image: repo:tag, CNPG's imageName: repo:tag@digest, a key named <x>Image - platform's rcloneImage, CNPG's ephemeralImage: missed until 2026-11-18, rclone 1.71.2 stood still)
A version kept beside its image (ScyllaCluster's version: with scylladb/scylla), annotated as the Ansible vars are

CI's copies of production's images: a CI check runs in the image production runs and refuses the two apart (platform's .woodpecker/alertmanager-render.sh and clickhouse-config-start.sh, infra's tests/stale-pr-envs-sweeper and tests/restore-check-age) - the step's image and its CI_STEP_IMAGE_CHECK moved with production's, digest kept, in the same branch: one depName, one update (a unit that moved production's alone stayed red: wave-patches 2026-11-16). These images alone - CI's own tools (helm, kubeconform, postgres, the scanner) are never a unit

Renovate's own image (scripts/upgrade-renovate.sh: image=renovate/renovate:<version>) - nothing watched it: 44.198.3 (2026-10-30) stood while 44.246.4 was out (2026-11-16) - pinned by digest too (a Docker Hub tag can move, and this image holds the bot's token: the wave-patches review, 2026-11-23)

packageRules.description: First-party images are promoted by GitOps (task promote:run), never by Renovate
kagent is disabled in production and left alone - nothing upgrades it
The retired in-cluster Vault's values: no Argo app reads them (Vault runs on the Pis - deploy/ansible/vars/vault.yml)
platform's Keycloak chart (schnappy-auth): no Argo app deploys it - Keycloak runs on the Pis (setup-pi-services.yml)
etcdctl for the backups follows the cluster's etcd, which kubeadm moves with Kubernetes: its patches only
The plain Kafka StatefulSet's image: off in production and the test environment (Strimzi runs Kafka - its version is strimzi.kafkaVersion), no pod runs it
Every patch and digest, every repo: one unit

Every minor in the same unit (operator 2026-11-23: a unit each was a week of runs for ~30 minors) - the stores' minors aside (scripts/upgrade-stores.json's packages, each its own unit; the harness checks the two lists alike), and the families below take theirs back: each of them names its branch by group.branchTopic, or this rule's would stay

Istio's minors together, one minor at a time - renovate/istio-<X.Y> (its Gateway API is a unit of its own, the next rule: named by its own version it made istio-1.6/istio-1.7, picked before istio-1.32)

The Gateway API (its CRDs, ops' gateway_api_version), one minor at a time - renovate/gateway-api-<X.Y>, picked after the Istio family's units (upgrade-units.py's FAMILIES); the copy's proof catches a Gateway API the Istio running does not support (operator 2026-11-16)
Kubernetes and the kubectl images beside it, one minor at a time - renovate/kubernetes-<X.Y> (its packages' apt repository moves with the minor)
Cilium, one minor at a time - renovate/cilium-<X.Y>
Observability's minors
The data operators and their stores' minors (Strimzi with Kafka, the Scylla operator and Manager with ScyllaDB)
ScyllaDB's release lines (2026.1 -> 2026.3: a minor by number, one-way by format) - renovate/scylladb-<X.Y>, one at a time, out of the data operators' unit
Argo CD alone
The Pis' services (their upgrade playbooks, one Pi at a time)
Kubernetes, Cilium, Istio and ScyllaDB's release lines: one minor at a time (each minor its own branch - the families above name it)
ClickHouse: the LTS lines only (YY.3, YY.8)
Forgejo: its LTS line only, patches until the next LTS (19, 2027-04) - operator 2026-10-05

Majors: proven, reviewed for compatibility (each step from the version running) and applied like any unit - one major a unit, the lower first (separateMultipleMajor); one-way ones take their stores' backup first (the cycle)

The majors that can be undone in one unit, renovate/wave-majors (operator 2026-11-23: a unit each was a day of runs for five) - each package's newest major alone (the next rule), the review judging every step's release notes; a store's major (scripts/upgrade-stores.json's packages: one-way, backed up first) and the release lines' (Kubernetes, Cilium, Istio, the Gateway API, ScyllaDB - the rule naming them above) each a unit of its own; the harness checks this list is those two

The wave's majors: each package's newest major alone (kube-prometheus-stack 91 -> 93, not 92 then 93) - two majors of one package in one branch collide and Renovate keeps either; the same packages as the rule above (without an update type: Renovate reads this before it knows one)

One-way majors (Postgres - the CNPG image ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql the databases run; the plain postgres image here is only the init-users Job's psql client and CI services, no store -, ScyllaDB, Kafka and Strimzi, ClickHouse, Grafana, Vault, Consul): label one-way - the runner backs the store up first or blocks the unit, naming the part with no backup (scripts/upgrade-stores.json: each package here a store's there, the harness checks)

SonarQube: every release migrates its database one way (api/system/migrate_db in the setup hook) - its patches, minors and majors a unit of their own, labelled one-way: the runner backs its CNPG cluster up first (scripts/upgrade-stores.json). It rode in the wave, unproven and with no backup (the wave-patches review, 2026-11-23)
The test environment's files: a unit of their own, renovate/test-<unit>, merged before its production twin (the Vagrant copy leaves the test environment out - it is its own proof)

ops' pinned build hashes move with their version, each read from what its vendor signs (scripts/renovate-checksums.py): a signature that does not check fails the task and leaves the old pins - copy-unit.sh's --check then refuses the unit, never a download unchecked. Once a branch, on every ops update: a branch's settings are its first update's (any of ops'), and per update each run would read every pin the branch moved again
Caddy on the Pis is Caddy's own apt package (setup-caddy.yml): its versions read from Cloudsmith's index, the Pis' architecture

Woodpecker, the CI server (its chart, and the server and agent images infra's values pin - registry and repository named there since 2026-11-21 so Renovate reads their tag; they move together): a unit of its own, renovate/manual-woodpecker - the Vagrant copy runs no Woodpecker, so nothing proves it there and the copy refuses it (SHADOW run 7, 2026-11-16). The runner never picks a manual- unit: applied by hand - infra's pull request merged, then ops' (setup-woodpecker.yml's woodpecker_chart_default moves with it), a pipeline run checked (a bad one is CI down, reverted by its commit), then production's inventory read again and committed (task test:copy:inventory) - ops' main fails defaults-follow-production from ops' merge until then, as after every applied unit until its record. Last, so it takes Woodpecker out of wave-patches and every group (operator 2026-11-16). Its group.branchTopic too: the wave-patches rule names its branch by one, and a groupSlug alone left Woodpecker on renovate/manual-wave-patches (SHADOW run 8, 2026-11-16)
